Case 4:24-cv-09138-HSG              Document 51      Filed 09/17/25      Page 1 of 3




                                   1

                                   2

                                   3

                                   4                                     UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

                                   5                                    NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

                                   6

                                   7     STEPHEN D. JOIN DIGITAL, INC., et al.,              Case No. 24-cv-09138-HSG
                                   8                      Plaintiffs,                        ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR
                                                                                             LEAVE TO AMEND
                                   9                v.
                                                                                             Re: Dkt. No. 33
                                  10     PIVIUM, INC.,
                                  11                      Defendant.

                                  12          Pending before the Court is Plaintiff’s motion for leave to file a second amended
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   complaint. Dkt. No. 33. For the following reasons, the Court GRANTS the motion.

                                  14          I.         BACKGROUND

                                  15          Plaintiff filed this action on December 17, 2024, bringing contract claims relating to

                                  16   Defendant’s installation of an audio visual system. See Dkt. No. 1. Plaintiff filed its first

                                  17   amended complaint on February 11, 2025, which added an exhibit that had been omitted from the

                                  18   original filing. See Dkt. No. 5. On June 4, 2025, the Court issued a scheduling order setting July

                                  19   30, 2025, as the deadline for Plaintiff to amend its pleadings. Dkt. No. 25. On June 24, 2025,

                                  20   Plaintiff filed a motion for leave to file a second amended complaint and explained that the

                                  21   amended complaint would add an additional negligence claim. See Dkt. No. 33 (“Mot.”).

                                  22   Defendant opposes. See Dkt. No. 37 (“Opp.”). The Court took the matter under submission

                                  23   without argument on July 18, 2025. Dkt. No. 39.

                                  24          II.        LEGAL STANDARD

                                  25          Since Plaintiff timely filed this request for leave to amend by the deadline in the

                                  26   scheduling order, the Court looks to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15 to determine whether

                                  27   amendment is appropriate. Under Rule 15(a)(1), “[a] party may amend its pleading once as a

                                  28   matter of course . . . 21 days after service of a motion under Rule 12(b) . . . .” Fed. R. Civ. P.
                                         Case 4:24-cv-09138-HSG           Document 51         Filed 09/17/25     Page 2 of 3




                                   1   15(a)(1)(B). Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(a)(2), “[i]n all other cases, a party may

                                   2   amend its pleading only with the opposing party’s written consent or the court’s leave.” Fed. R.

                                   3   Civ. P. 15(a)(2). “[L]eave to amend shall be freely granted ‘when justice so requires.’” Townsend

                                   4   v. Univ. of Alaska, 543 F.3d 478, 485 (9th Cir. 2008) (quoting Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2)). “This

                                   5   policy is to be applied with extreme liberality.” Eminence Capital, LLC v. Aspeon, Inc., 316 F.3d

                                   6   1048, 1051 (9th Cir. 2003) (quotation omitted). When considering whether to grant leave to

                                   7   amend, the court considers several factors, including (1) bad faith, (2) undue delay, (3) prejudice

                                   8   to the opposing party, (4) futility of amendment, and (5) previous amendments. See Foman v.

                                   9   Davis, 371 U.S. 178, 182 (1962). The Court weighs prejudice to the opposing party most heavily.

                                  10   Eminence Capital, 316 F.3d at 1052. “Absent prejudice, or a strong showing of any of the

                                  11   remaining Foman factors, there exists a presumption under Rule 15(a) in favor of granting leave to

                                  12   amend.” Id. (emphasis in original).
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          III.    DISCUSSION

                                  14          Upon considering the relevant factors, the Court finds that leave to file a second amended

                                  15   complaint should be granted under this circuit’s liberal standard.

                                  16          Defendant argues that it will be prejudiced by amendment because it will “be forced to

                                  17   expend time and resources on moving to dismiss the claim,” and argues that the proposed

                                  18   amendment will “expand the scope of the case in the midst of the parties exchanging discovery,

                                  19   taking depositions and preparing for the upcoming mediation.” Opp. at 5. The Court disagrees.

                                  20   Plaintiffs seek to add a negligence claim based on substantially the same material facts already

                                  21   alleged in prior complaints. The essence of the case remains what it has been from the beginning:

                                  22   a dispute involving installation of an audio visual project. See Dkt. No. 38 (“Reply”) at 8. And in

                                  23   any event, the expansion of a case due to the addition of new causes of action is not inherently

                                  24   prejudicial.

                                  25          Given the absence of prejudice, there must be a strong showing of the other Foman factors

                                  26   to overcome Rule 15’s strong presumption in favor of granting leave to amend. But Defendant

                                  27   has not met this burden. Defendant primarily argues that Plaintiff’s proposed amendments are

                                  28   futile because the negligence claim is barred by the economic loss rule. Opp. at 2. Leave to
                                                                                         2
                                         Case 4:24-cv-09138-HSG            Document 51        Filed 09/17/25      Page 3 of 3




                                   1   amend should be denied as futile only when “no set of facts can be proved under the amendment

                                   2   to the pleadings that would constitute a valid and sufficient claim or defense.” Missouri ex rel.

                                   3   Koster v. Harris, 847 F.3d 646, 656 (9th Cir. 2017) (quotation omitted). Courts rarely deny leave

                                   4   to amend based on futility and instead generally “defer consideration of challenges to the merits of

                                   5   a proposed amended pleading until after leave to amend is granted and the amended pleading is

                                   6   filed.” Gregg v. Monastery Camp, No. 23-CV-02760-AMO, 2024 WL 2304564, at *2 (N.D. Cal.

                                   7   May 21, 2024) (quotation omitted). Since “[t]he merits or facts of a controversy are not properly

                                   8   decided in a motion for leave to amend and should instead be attacked by a motion to dismiss for

                                   9   failure to state a claim or for summary judgment,” the Court will not deny leave to amend here on

                                  10   futility grounds. LiveCareer Ltd. v. Su Jia Techs. Ltd., No. 14-CV-03336-JST, 2015 WL

                                  11   4089800, at *3 (N.D. Cal. July 2, 2015) (quotation omitted).

                                  12            Additionally, Defendant implies that Plaintiff delayed in seeking amendment. See Opp. at
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   5. But Plaintiff sought leave to file the amended complaint by the Court’s deadline. And “[t]he

                                  14   mere fact that an amendment is offered late in the case . . . is not enough to bar it.” United States

                                  15   v. Webb, 655 F.2d 977, 980 (9th Cir. 1981) (quotation omitted).

                                  16            For these reasons, the Court finds leave to amend the complaint to be warranted. If

                                  17   Defendant continues to believe that this claim is barred by the economic loss rule, it should

                                  18   promptly raise those arguments in a motion to dismiss.

                                  19            IV.      CONCLUSION

                                  20            The Court GRANTS Plaintiff’s motion for leave to amend the complaint, Dkt. No. 33.

                                  21   Plaintiff shall file its second amended complaint on the docket within three days from the date of

                                  22   this order.

                                  23

                                  24            IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  25   Dated:        9/17/2025

                                  26                                                    ______________________________________
                                                                                        HAYWOOD S. GILLIAM, JR.
                                  27                                                    United States District Judge
